author: lax leader
title: Tommy Edman returns to Dodgers lineup as team seeks sweep against Rays
text:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are aiming for a series sweep against the Tampa Bay Rays in Wednesday afternoon’s game at Dodger Stadium, with Tommy Edman making his return to the lineup on June 17. Edman, who has missed the entire 2026 season so far, will lead off and play third base for the Dodgers.
Edman’s return comes as the Dodgers look to build on their recent 1-0 win over the Rays on Tuesday night. The team currently holds a record of 47-27, while the Rays stand at 41-29. Shohei Ohtani is set to start as pitcher for Los Angeles in this series finale but will not be hitting. Ohtani enters this game with a 6-2 record and an earned run average of 1.06 for the season, having recorded 73 strikeouts and a WHIP of 0.842 so far.
Manager Dave Roberts has adjusted the batting order following Edman’s return, moving Miguel Rojas into the designated hitter spot. The starting lineup features Andy Pages batting second in center field, Freddie Freeman at first base batting third, and Mookie Betts at shortstop in the cleanup position. Rojas bats fifth, followed by Kyle Tucker in right field.
Alex Call is set to play left field and bat seventh, with Dalton Rushing catching after being replaced by Chuckie Robinson on Tuesday. Alex Freeland rounds out the order at second base, batting ninth.
For Tampa Bay, Shane McClanahan will start as pitcher. McClanahan holds a season record of six wins and four losses with an earned run average of 3.23 and has tallied 66 strikeouts.
The game begins at 12:10 p.m. Pacific Time and will be broadcast on SportsNet LA.
